Glubczyce Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Głubczyce, Poland

Demolished. Głubczyce's original Jewish cemetery (see the Głubczyce New Jewish Cemetery record for the town's fuller community history) was established in 1814 following regulations requiring cemeteries near Jewish residential areas, with additional land purchased and a fence added in 1868. Ownership transferred to the Reich Association in 1939, then to the Gestapo in 1943, which completely destroyed the site; recovered matzevot fragments were used to pave a municipal-office courtyard wall. Authorities converted the grounds into a public square in 1965.
